title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: There exists a constant $c$ such that for any positive integers $n$ and $\kappa_1 \geq \cdots \geq \kappa_n$, the partition polytope $\mathrm{PP}(\kappa_1, \ldots, \kappa_n)$ has diameter at most $\lceil 4\kappa_1/3 \rceil + c$.
context_text: For nonnegative integers $\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_n$ with $\kappa_1+\dots+\kappa_n=m$, the partition polytope $\mathrm{PP}(\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_n)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{nm}$ is defined by $\sum_{j=1}^m y_{ij}=\kappa_i$ for every $i\le n$, $\sum_{i=1}^n y_{ij}=1$ for every $j\le m$, and $y_{ij}\ge0$; its vertices are exactly the incidence matrices of the assignments $p:[m]\to[n]$ of $m$ items to $n$ clusters with cluster sizes $\kappa_1,\dots,\kappa_n$. Its (combinatorial) diameter is the diameter of its edge graph (the graph of vertices and edges of the polytope). Two vertices $p,p'$ are adjacent if and only if their clustering difference graph (the digraph on the clusters $[n]$ with an arc from $p(j)$ to $p'(j)$ for each item $j$, loops suppressed) is a single directed cycle, i.e. $p'$ is obtained from $p$ by one cyclic exchange of items between clusters; so the diameter is the maximum, over pairs of assignments of the same shape, of the minimum number of cyclic exchanges transforming one into the other. Partition polytopes generalise Birkhoff polytopes ($n=m$, all $\kappa_i=1$, diameter $2$). Borgwardt showed the diameter is at most $\kappa_1+\kappa_2$; the authors improve this to $\kappa_1+\lceil\kappa_2/2\rceil\le\lceil3\kappa_1/2\rceil$ (and to $3$ when $\kappa_1=2$), while the known lower bound, noted by Borgwardt, is $\lceil4\kappa_1/3\rceil$. They suspect the true value is closer to the lower bound; the natural approach of proving diameter at most $4$ when $\kappa_1=3$ fails, as they show by an explicit example, so new techniques would be needed.
paper_title: Improved Decomposition Bounds for Partition Polytopes and Odd-Covers
